properties.title: SurgVista: Long-Horizon Surgical World Modeling with Plausible Instrument-Tissue Dynamics

membership.reason: Action-conditioned surgical video DiT (Wan2.1-1.3B + DCR + DAT) rolling out up to 800 frames conditioned on instrument keypoint trajectories.

properties.backbone: Wan2.1-1.3B LoRA flow-matching video DiT with Latent Action Encoding, DCR InfoNCE, and DAT

properties.flow: Initial frame s_0 + instrument keypoint trajectories a_{1:T} -> Latent Action Encoding M + Autoregressive DiT clip rollouts -> VAE decoder -> 80/800-frame surgical video

properties.purpose: Long-horizon action-conditioned surgical scene simulation for robot policy development and evaluation.
properties.environment: Retrospective surgical video benchmarks (GraSP, SurgToolLoc22, CholecTrack20)

evidence_fragments.content: We present SurgVista, a surgical world model that mitigates both failures through two training recipes. Deformation Consistency Regularization extracts scene-point trajectories from training videos and enforces cross-frame coherence through latent contrastive learning, strengthening physically consistent instrument-tissue dynamics.

locator.section_or_table: Section 3 SurgVista Problem Formulation and Overview

evidence_fragments.content: Problem Formulation. Given an observed frame s0 ∈R H×W×3 and an action sequence a1:T , SurgVista predicts future frames ˆs1:T that capture both instrument motion and the induced tissue deformation. For long-horizon simulation beyond a single clip, generated clips are chained autoregressively, where the tail frames of each generated clip condition the next.
SurgVista instead converts instrument keypoint trajectories into an action latent by replicating first-frame latent features along each trajectory [ 10].

Procedural diversity. SurgWorld-Bench draws from three public datasets covering three surgical procedure types (Fig. 4a): GraSP [ 2] for radical prostatectomy, SurgToolLoc22 [ 40] for porcine laparoscopic procedures, and CholecTrack20 [ 26] for laparoscopic cholecystectomy, collectively encompassing diverse subjects, heterogeneous instrument types, and varied tissue biomechanics.

The benchmark operates at two evaluation horizons (Fig. 4a): a short horizon of 80 frames over 111 evaluation clips for comparability with prior work, and a long horizon of 800 frames over 21 evaluation clips to probe long-horizon stability.

To condition generation on instrument actions, each action at is represented as a set of instrument keypoint coordinates, forming trajectories {pk1:T }Kk=1 that specify instrument positions over time. Latent Action Encoding (Sec. 3.1) converts these trajectories into an action latent M by replicating first-frame latent features at each trajectory’s target positions. The action latent M is concatenated with zτ along the channel dimension, while zfirst =E(s 0) is projected through a reference convolution into tokens prepended to the DiT input sequence.
An InfoNCE loss [8, 17] then pulls each descriptor toward its own prototype while pushing it away from the prototypes of the remaining J−1 trajectories:

Motivated by this observation, we randomly apply four photometric perturbations to the conditioning frame: exposure shift, contrast jitter, sharpness scaling, and noise adjustment, each with randomly sampled strength calibrated to match observed rollout artifacts.
SurgVista builds on Wan2.1-1.3B and is trained for 100K iterations at 512×320 resolution with a clip length of 81 frames.

The instrument-region scores measure whether predicted instruments follow the prescribed action a1:T , while the tissue-region scores measure whether the induced deformation matches the ground-truth interaction.

capability_assessments.rationale: Action-conditioned surgical video DiT rolling out up to 800 frames conditioned on instrument keypoint trajectories, evaluated on instrument-motion and tissue-response fidelity.

limitations: No alternative-action comparison or downstream robot policy learning evaluated.
No uncertainty quantification or prospective surgical study.
